name: Autosomal Dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease Type 2D
aliases: Distal Hereditary Motor Neuropathy Type V

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for CMT2D

criteria.description: Presence of distal motor and sensory neuropathy with predominant distal muscle weakness and atrophy
Electrophysiological evidence of axonal neuropathy with reduced compound muscle action potentials and normal or mildly reduced nerve conduction velocities
Identification of pathogenic heterozygous mutation in the GARS gene
Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with affected first-degree relatives
Muscle biopsy showing neurogenic atrophy (if performed)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of distal motor and sensory neuropathy with electrophysiological evidence of axonal neuropathy plus identification of a pathogenic GARS mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for confirmation; clinical presentation can overlap with other CMT subtypes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Distal muscle weakness and atrophy predominantly affecting hands
searchTerms: shrinking muscles in fingers and hands

pathognomonic.symptomName: Sensory loss in distal extremities (glove and stocking distribution)
searchTerms: numbness in glove and stocking pattern
sensory loss in hands and feet
reduced feeling in fingers and toes

common.symptomName: Hyporeflexia or areflexia in lower limbs

searchTerms: tingling sensations in hands and feet
abnormal sensations in fingers and toes
mild stiff joints in fingers or toes
slight joint tightening in hands or feet

occasional.symptomName: Mild distal sensory loss in upper limbs

searchTerms: difficulty breathing due to muscle weakness

laboratory: Elevated creatine kinase may be mild or absent
imaging: Muscle MRI may show distal muscle atrophy and fatty infiltration
other: Electromyography showing chronic denervation and reinnervation
Nerve conduction studies consistent with axonal neuropathy

distinguishingFeatures: Pure motor neuropathy without sensory loss
Mutations in GARS or other genes

redFlags: Rapid progression of weakness over weeks to months
Early onset severe sensory loss or autonomic dysfunction
references: Rossor AM, Polke JM, Houlden H, Reilly MM. Clinical implications of genetic advances in Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease. Nat Rev Neurol. 2013;9(10):562-571.

Antonellis A, Ellsworth RE, Sambuughin N, et al. Glycyl-tRNA synthetase mutations in Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2D and distal spinal muscular atrophy type V. Am J Hum Genet. 2003;72(5):1293-1299.
